᠁ ᠸᠢᠨᠠᠶ᠎ᠠ ᠳ᠋ᠤ ᠨᠣᠮᠯᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠂ ᠬᠡᠵᠢᠶ᠎ᠡ
ᠴᠠᠭ ᠢ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠨ ᠤᠬᠠᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠄
ᠭᠡᠰᠦ ᠢ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠨ ᠤᠬᠠᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠄
ᠵᠣᠭᠣᠭ ᠢ ᠢᠯᠭᠠᠨ ᠤᠬᠠᠭᠳᠠᠬᠤᠢ ᠂ ᠭᠡᠰᠡᠨ
ᠡᠳᠡ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠵᠦ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠢ
ᠢᠳᠡ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠨᠣᠮᠯᠠᠪᠠ ᠄
ᠡᠨᠡ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠬᠦ ᠭᠡᠰᠡᠨ ᠂
ᠶᠠᠮᠠᠷ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠬᠦ ᠄
ᠥ᠍ᠪᠡᠷ ᠦᠨ ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠤ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠢ ᠤ
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢ ᠄ ᠮᠦᠨ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ
ᠪᠦᠲᠦᠭᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠮᠢᠬ᠎ᠠ ᠴᠢᠰᠤ ᠵᠢᠴᠢ ᠂
ᠶᠠᠰᠤ ᠵᠢᠷᠦᠭᠡ ᠡᠯᠢᠭᠡ ᠠᠭᠤᠰᠬᠢ
ᠭᠡᠳᠡᠰᠦ ᠭᠦᠵᠡ ᠭᠡᠰᠡᠨ ᠡᠳᠡ ᠨᠤᠭᠤᠳ ᠄
ᠠᠮᠢᠨ ᠢ ᠲᠡᠵᠢᠶᠡᠬᠦ ᠳ᠋ᠤ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠥ᠍ᠭᠭᠦᠭᠡᠳ ᠂
ᠡᠪᠡᠳᠴᠢᠨ ᠢ ᠠᠷᠢᠯᠭᠠᠬᠤ ᠲᠤ ᠡᠮ
ᠵᠢᠴᠢ ᠂ ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ ᠳ᠋ᠤ ᠬᠡᠷᠡᠭᠯᠡᠬᠦ ᠡᠳ᠋
ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠵᠦ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠢᠳᠡᠬᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ
ᠠᠮᠢ ᠪᠡᠶ᠎ᠡ ᠂ ᠨᠠᠰᠤ ᠢ ᠤᠷᠲᠤᠳᠬᠠᠵᠤ
ᠴᠢᠳᠠᠬᠤ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠮᠤᠢ ᠂ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠨ ᠡᠨᠡ
ᠨᠢᠭᠡ ᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠵᠦ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠢ ᠢᠳᠡ ᠄
ᠳ᠋ᠠᠷᠠᠭ᠎ᠠ ᠨᠢ ᠵᠣᠭᠣᠭ ᠤᠨ ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠢ
ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠵᠦ ᠢᠳᠡ ᠭᠡᠰᠡᠨ ᠪᠣᠯᠪᠠᠰᠤ ᠂

<margin><term>ja doloɣan degedü qoyar</term> <gloss>Section Ja, Volume Seven, Upper Part, Folio Two</gloss></margin>

It is taught in the <term>Vinaya</term> <gloss>monastic discipline</gloss>:
"Distinguish and understand the proper time;
distinguish and understand the belly <note>original: "gesü", meaning the stomach or digestive capacity</note>;
distinguish and understand the meal <note>original: "joɣoɣ"</note>;
knowing these three, partake of food," thus it was taught.
As for this "knowing,"
what nature <note>original: "činar"</note> is to be known?
Knowing the nature of what abides within one's own body:
namely, the flesh and blood that constitute this very body, as well as
the bones, heart, liver, lungs,
intestines, and stomach <note>original: "güje"</note>; all of these.
By giving food to nourish life,
and by knowing food as medicine to dispel illness
and as a substance necessary for the body, if one partakes of food in this manner,
one will be able to prolong one's life, body, and years of age.
Knowing this first point, partake of food.
Next, as for the teaching "know the food of the meal and eat,"
it means knowing the nature of <unclear>ᠢᠳᠡᠭᠡᠨ ᠦ</unclear> and eating,

<margin>The Sutra of Various Sections, Volume Seven, Upper Part, Folio Two <note>original: "諸品經第七卷上二"</note></margin>

<summary>This folio from the seventh volume of a Mongolian Buddhist canonical collection presents instructions from the Vinaya on mindful eating. It explains that a practitioner must understand the proper time, the capacity of the stomach, and the nature of the meal, viewing food as medicine to sustain the physical organs and prolong life.</summary>
<keywords>Vinaya, monastic discipline, mindful eating, Buddhist medicine, bodily organs, Classical Mongolian, sutra, food as medicine</keywords>
